item.title: Delta govt imposes curfew in Ughelli North after campaign rally violence
item.description: The Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area following reported violence at a campaign rally of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Uduere Community, which allegedly left some people dead and several others injured. The curfew, which takes effect from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily, will remain in force until further notice. The Delta State Police Command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bright Edafe. According to the statement, the police have commenced investigations to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible. The Command urged residents to comply strictly with the curfew and cooperate with security personnel to maintain peace and public safety. The statement reads, “The Command therefore urges residents of Ughelli North Local Government Area to comply strictly with the curfew imposed by the Delta State Government, restricting movement between 1800hrs to 0600hrs until further notice. Residents are advised to remain calm and cooperate with security personnel in the interest of public safety. “The Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, CP Samuel E. Erale, psc, mnips, has directed intensified security operations in the affected area to prevent further violence and maintain law and order. The CP has ordered a full-scale investigation and assures residents of the state that anyone found culpable will face the full weight of the law, irrespective of political affiliation or status, and urges members of the public to provide credible information to assist ongoing investigations.” Erale also extended his condolences to the families of those who died and wished the injured a speedy recovery. He reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to protecting lives and property while ensuring a peaceful environment for lawful political activities. The police commissioner further warned political actors and their supporters against thuggery, intimidation and the unlawful use of firearms. He stressed that political differences must never be allowed to degenerate into violence or loss of lives. item.title: 89 fall ill after unknown substance released at UK Arena concert
item.description: Thousands of concertgoers were evacuated from the UK’s largest indoor arena after the release of an “unknown substance”, with dozens reporting suffering side effects, police said Monday. Some 12,000 people were attending the Sunday night show by US rapper Don Toliver at the Co-op Live arena in Manchester, northwest England. “A total of 89 people displayed symptoms believed to be linked to exposure,” Manchester police said, adding one woman was taken to hospital for treatment. “Enquiries remain ongoing to establish the nature of the substance, where it came from and any associated risk,” Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said in a statement. Toliver said he had postponed his Monday night London show following the incident, which led to one person being taken to hospital. Emergency services were called after “reports of people in the crowd suffering effects from an unknown substance”, Manchester police said, declaring a major incident at the scene. The venue, which bills itself as the country’s largest live entertainment arena, said it was working with police to “identify the cause of the incident”. The regional ambulance service said it assessed more than 50 people, including some reporting “eye and respiratory symptoms”. Toliver, who was nominated for five Grammy Awards last week, is currently on the second leg of his “Nitrous” world tour. He announced he was rescheduling his show at London’s O2 arena due to an “unfortunate incident last night (in) Manchester”. “My heart and prayers are with everyone that was injured last night,” Toliver said on Instagram, without providing more details. Concertgoers told the BBC that people were “choking” and coughing, recalling “distressing scenes” of people leaving the venue in a panic. Some criticised the lack of security checks at the venue, especially in a city still scarred by the 2017 Manchester Arena bombing, which killed 22 people at an Ariana Grande concert. item.title: 2027: Armed Men Who Killed Four NDC Campaign Members Said I Was Their Target, Omo-Agege
item.description: Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege has alleged that the gunmen who attacked his campaign team in Delta State, killing four people, repeatedly shouted his name and declared their intention to kill him. Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central Senatorial District on the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 general elections, said he escaped the attack through the intervention of his Department of State Services (DSS) escorts. He spoke on Monday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today . ﻿ Recounting the incident, the former deputy senate president said he heard the attackers repeatedly shouting that they wanted to kill him while opening fire at the campaign venue. “Right there at the venue, while they were shooting, we could hear them say, ‘It is Omo-Agege we want to kill. We must kill Omo-Agege.’ “But I was lucky because my DSS details were very professional. In fact, after God, the only reason I am alive today is because of the DSS operatives who were with me,” he said. Omo-Agege described the incident as a premeditated attack, alleging that there had been a build-up to the violence. He questioned why he would be singled out for elimination when several other politicians were also contesting elective positions. The former lawmaker said the attackers struck less than five minutes after he began addressing supporters at the campaign venue. According to him, he had moved towards the side of his vehicle to make eye contact with members of the audience when the gunshots rang out. “It was by divine intervention. As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of the vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started,” he said. The former deputy senate president said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others sustained injuries, with some in critical condition. ﻿ In a statement issued earlier on Monday by his media adviser, Sunny Areh, Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation said he survived an assassination attempt during a campaign tour in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. Areh alleged that armed men opened fire on the senator and his entourage while he was addressing supporters during a campaign visit. The organisation called for an independent and thorough investigation by the Nigeria Police Force, while appealing to the Inspector-General of Police, the DSS, INEC, civil society organisations and the international community to ensure the safety of political candidates and their supporters. It also urged supporters to remain calm and avoid retaliation, adding that its ward-to-ward campaign activities across Delta Central would continue. item.title: Caregiver Salami shot dead in US weeks before starting Nursing school
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye A 24-year-old Togolese caregiver in Chicago, Bintou Salami, has been shot dead while returning home from work, weeks before she was due to begin nursing school. According to ABC7 Chicago, Salami was found with a gunshot wound in the 1400 block of West Chase Avenue at about 11:15 p.m. on Wednesday. She had just finished her shift at Misericordia, where she cared for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Ms Salami relocated from France to the U.S. in 2024 following her marriage and planned to begin nursing school in January; she is survived by her husband and son. Her killing was one of three shootings on Chicago’s North Side that night as Police said the incidents were connected. A 35-year-old man was critically wounded near the bike path by Belmont Harbor, while a 25-year-old man was later found dead at the Morse Red Line station and a gun was recovered at the station. The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office said the man died by suicide. Salami’s coworkers described her as caring and devoted. Ashley Hespen, assistant vice president of residential services at Misericordia, said residents loved spending time with her. Friends, relatives and members of Chicago’s Togolese community gathered at a vigil to honour Salami and demand answers. As they sang the Togolese national anthem, supporters stood with her brother at the place where she was killed. “I can’t stop looking at the picture. I don’t know, like — it’s not fair,” said Nanipo Damyete, Salami’s former roommate. Amevi Avouglah, the USA country delegate for the High Council of Togolese Abroad, said Salami’s future had been cut short. “All the dreams that Bintou is carrying vanished like that in one minute! She was coming from work,” Avouglah said. Salami’s brother, Raoufou, questioned the suggestion that she was killed during a robbery, saying nothing appeared to have been taken. “The police telling me, like, somebody tried to rob her or something. What I can’t understand is how are you trying to rob somebody and you don’t take her phone, nothing?” he said. Salami moved to the United States from France in 2024 after completing college and following her marriage. She is survived by her husband and their 4-year-old son, who lives with her mother in Togo. Chicago police have not publicly explained how the shootings were connected and no suspects have been identified. The fatal shooting has sparked calls for justice from her family, friends and members of the Togolese community in the U.S. Vanguard News The post Caregiver Salami shot dead in US weeks before starting Nursing school appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: PSG suffer major injury blow as Doue, Kvaratskhelia face long layoffs
item.description: The sight of the unfortunate Desire Doue going down holding his knee in agony was distressing for anyone connected to Paris Saint-Germain, but encouraging for those hoping to stop the French club from winning a third consecutive Champions League this season. PSG have been European champions in each of the last two years and their quest to retain the crown this season has started superbly, with four straight wins leaving them top of the 36-team standings halfway through the league phase. However, they have now lost the outstanding Doue, exactly a month after Khvicha Kvaratskhelia succumbed to the same injury, casting serious doubt over the chances of Luis Enrique’s team going all the way again. Doue was stretchered off in tears after twisting his knee awkwardly during PSG’s 3-2 win at Nice in Ligue 1 on Saturday, with the club later confirming the 21-year-old had ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee and needed surgery. Doue’s season is likely now over, while Kvaratskhelia is beginning the process of rehabilitation after rupturing the same ACL in last month’s win over Barcelona. The explosive Georgian winger was the best player in last season’s Champions League knockout rounds and came sixth in this year’s Ballon d’Or ranking. Meanwhile Doue was the man of the match when Paris demolished Inter Milan 5-0 in the 2025 Champions League final and had been their star performer in recent weeks. “He will come back twice as strong. I am not worried,” insisted Luis Enrique, but he will know that the injuries to two of his best attacking players seriously damage the club’s prospects of more European glory. So what do they do now, as they prepare to host Roma on Wednesday and with the January transfer window approaching? “We are always open to possibilities in the transfer window, but not just because we have players injured,” said the Spaniard. “We have players who can come in and we will overcome this as a team. It is not a problem.” He could be forgiven for now regretting the decision to allow Bradley Barcola — scorer of 34 goals across the last two campaigns — to leave for Liverpool. Suddenly the pressure on the injury-prone Ousmane Dembele to stay fit is enormous. – Bayern in bother – As for who appears the best-placed to take advantage of PSG’s misfortune, it may not be Bayern Munich, as the German champions deal with problems of their own. Twenty-four hours before Doue went down for PSG, newly-crowned Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane was substituted with an ankle injury playing for Bayern against Cologne. He is now expected to be sidelined for up to four months, although that will at least mean he has a chance of being fresh by March, in time for the Champions League knockout rounds. “I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season,” Kane said in a social media post. item.title: Sinner set to undergo knee surgery, might miss Australian Open
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Former world number one Jannik Sinner is set to undergo knee surgery in Finland, a development that could rule him out of the 2027 Australian Open, according to Sky Sports Italia. The Italian tennis star could be sidelined for between three and four months following the procedure, which is expected to be performed by Lasse Lempainen, a specialist in tendon and muscle injuries. Sinner, 25, has been struggling with persistent inflammation in his right knee, which forced him to end his 2026 season prematurely. His last competitive appearance was at Wimbledon in July, where he defeated Alexander Zverev in the final to win his fifth Grand Slam title. He subsequently missed the North American hard-court tournaments, including the US Open, because of the injury. The former world number one had earlier expressed hope of returning to action at the Australian Open in January, following a planned appearance at the Six Kings Slam in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in late December. “The goal is to go to Australia; I hope to get there, and perhaps play a few tournaments beforehand,” Sinner told reporters in Milan earlier this month. However, the reported surgery and expected recovery period have cast serious doubt over his participation in the season’s first Grand Slam. Despite competing in only nine tournaments during the 2026 season, Sinner recorded 44 wins in 47 matches, won six titles and reclaimed the world number one ranking during a 30-match winning streak. He also won his maiden titles at Indian Wells, Monte Carlo and Madrid, becoming the second man after Novak Djokovic to win all nine ATP Masters 1000 tournaments. Sinner ended his season in October and recently announced his separation from coach Darren Cahill after a successful five-year partnership. Magnus Norman has been tipped to replace the Australian. item.title: Alleged assassination: We want IG to investigate, not Delta police — Omo-Agege
item.description: Former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, has called on the Inspector-General of Police to take over the investigation into the alleged assassination attempt on him in Delta State, saying he has no confidence in the state police command to deliver justice. Omo-Agege, the Nigeria Democratic Congress senatorial candidate for Delta Central, made the appeal on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, following an attack on his campaign entourage in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area. He alleged that police officers present during the incident failed to intervene as gunmen opened fire on his team, adding that the attack had heightened fears among opposition politicians in the state. “What we have learned is this: we are not safe here in Delta State. In fact, all members of the opposition party, NDC, most especially, we are all endangered,” he said. Omo-Agege claimed that six truckloads of policemen were deployed to the campaign venue but did not act when the shooting occurred. He accused the state police command of being unlikely to conduct an impartial investigation and urged the IGP to handle the case directly. “We do not expect any justice to come from the police here in Delta State. Neither do we expect any justice to come from the police on this very one,” he said. “We are appealing to the IG to take this matter over directly. We tried to reach him this evening. We couldn’t reach him.” The former lawmaker said he wanted the federal police leadership to investigate the incident, insisting that the state command should not be involved in the probe. He also called for justice for those affected by the attack, saying lives had been lost and several others were receiving treatment in hospitals. “We need justice. We need justice. We need justice for these four people who have been killed. We need justice for the 15 people who are critically injured and hospitalised right now,” Omo-Agege said. Despite the incident, he vowed not to abandon his campaign, dismissing suggestions that the attack could intimidate him into withdrawing from the race. “If the idea is that this is supposed to deter me from going forward with the campaigns, it’s a very big mistake and a big lie. Ain’t going to happen,” he said. He, however, appealed to his supporters to remain calm and avoid reprisals, warning that tensions remained high following the attack. item.title: Osun police bust child trafficking syndicate, rescue 16-day-old baby
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Osun State Police Command has dismantled a suspected child trafficking syndicate and rescued a 16-day-old baby boy allegedly sold for N1.5 million in a transaction involving two suspects. The command’s Public Relations Officer, DSP Abiodun Ojelabi, disclosed this in a statement on Monday, saying two suspects had been arrested in connection with the alleged trafficking. According to the police, the baby’s mother, Victoria Michael, 18, gave birth at a private hospital in Kajola on November 2 but was unable to cater for the child after the father, identified as Tayo, allegedly denied responsibility. Ojelabi said one of the mother’s friends, Comfort Olayinka, offered to help her find assistance through a contact in Abeokuta, Ogun State. He said Olayinka subsequently linked up with Oladipo Olamide, 46, who allegedly claimed to operate a non-governmental organisation providing care for less-privileged persons and offered to take the baby into its care. The police spokesman said the baby’s mother and Olayinka travelled to Abeokuta on November 5 and handed the child over to Olamide. However, Olayinka later allegedly told the mother that the baby had died and gave her a folded object resembling a baby, packed in a bag, which she was instructed to throw into Lafenwa River. Unknown to the mother, Olayinka had allegedly collected N450,000 from Olamide, purportedly for her upkeep. Ojelabi said police operatives, acting on intelligence, arrested Olamide in Abeokuta on November 17. During interrogation, the suspect allegedly confessed to selling the baby to one Mrs Bolanle Ruth for N1.5 million. He said Olamide subsequently led the operatives to Akure, Ondo State, where Ruth was arrested on November 18. According to the police, Ruth admitted paying N1.5 million for the baby and claimed she was promised that the necessary documents would be provided by an agency, but had yet to receive them. The police did not disclose the whereabouts or status of the other suspect, Olayinka, in the statement. Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police in Osun State, Ibrahim Zungura, warned individuals and groups against child trafficking, assuring residents that the command would not tolerate the crime. He urged members of the public to provide useful information to security agencies to help prevent child trafficking and protect vulnerable children. item.title: Navy intercepts 89,000 litres of stolen crude, illegal diesel in Rivers
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Navy has intercepted about 35,000 litres of suspected stolen crude oil and uncovered an illegal refining site containing an additional 54,000 litres of suspected illegally refined Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) in Rivers State. The operation, conducted on November 22 by personnel of Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Pathfinder around Okarki Creek and Okarki Community in Ahoada West Local Government Area, followed credible intelligence. In a statement on Monday, the Director of Naval Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, said the naval personnel intercepted a wooden boat conveying about 150 sacks containing suspected stolen crude oil. He said a subsequent operation in the adjoining area led to the discovery of an illegal refining site containing approximately 10 dugout pits, 180 sacks and a storage container holding an estimated 54,000 litres of suspected illegally refined AGO. According to him, the combined volume of petroleum products recovered or identified during the operation was approximately 89,000 litres. “The boat, its contents and the refining site, including the stored products, were handled in accordance with established anti-crude oil theft procedures,” the statement said. The Navy described the operation as part of its sustained campaign to disrupt the supply networks supporting crude oil theft and illegal refining activities in the Niger Delta. It said intercepting the suspected stolen crude oil and dismantling associated refining infrastructure would help deny oil thieves access to petroleum resources while addressing environmental degradation and revenue losses. The Service reaffirmed its commitment to intelligence-driven operations to protect critical oil and gas infrastructure, support national crude oil production and safeguard Nigeria’s economic interests. It added that operations would continue across the Niger Delta creeks to combat crude oil theft and illegal refining. item.title: Bayelsa boat mishap death toll rises to 32, AIG visits scene
item.description: …Urges enforcement of life jacket, passenger capacity regulations By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of Zone 16, Regina Udoette, has visited Ayama-Ijaw waterside in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State following the boat mishap that claimed 32 lives. Udoette, who was accompanied by the Bayelsa State Commissioner of Police, Saka Ajao Adewale, visited the area on Monday to interact with marine transport workers and the Red Cross rescue team and receive updates on the ongoing search and recovery operation. During the visit, reports from the rescue site indicated that additional bodies had been recovered, raising the death toll from 29 to 32. The AIG commiserated with the Bayelsa State Government and residents over the tragedy, while commending President Bola Tinubu for his response and expression of sympathy following the incident. She expressed concern over alleged violations of maritime safety regulations, particularly the overloading of the vessel and failure to comply with life jacket requirements. According to her, the boat reportedly conveyed more than 500 passengers despite having a carrying capacity of 200. Udoette urged the state Ministry of Transport and marine unions to strengthen enforcement of safety regulations, particularly compulsory life jacket use and compliance with approved passenger limits. She also called for strict enforcement against operators who flout safety rules, stressing that passengers must take personal responsibility for their safety. Speaking with journalists, the AIG said she visited the waterside on behalf of the Inspector-General of Police to sympathise with the victims’ families and assess the situation. “I am here with my management team and the Bayelsa CP on behalf of the Inspector General of Police to sympathise with the people that died in the incident. I register our condolences and wish the injured quick recovery. “Besides, the maritime personnel told us of the refusal of passengers to obey safety rules, and the boat captain loaded over 500 persons for a boat with a 200-person capacity. That was a suicide mission and a disaster waiting to happen,” she said. Describing the deaths as avoidable, Udoette urged passengers and marine transport operators to comply with established safety regulations. “Some of these deaths are avoidable deaths. Many of the passengers refuse to obey safety rules. My Bible tells me obedience is better than sacrifice. There are rules and regulations on life jackets and overloading, but they refused. “For the living, this is a big lesson to everyone that wants to use a boat for their journey. They should listen to the rules. People should use common sense. This disaster is avoidable,” she added. She said Early Infant Diagnosis coverage among HIV-exposed infants increased from 15 per cent in 2022 to 66 per cent in 2025. “While this is significant progress, we must do more to ensure that no child is left behind,” Ilori said. She said the 2026 World AIDS Day theme, “Ending AIDS Starts with Access: Equity, Ownership and Sustainability,” highlighted the need for equitable access to HIV prevention, testing, treatment and care. “Access must not depend on where you live, what you earn or who you are. It is a right, not a privilege,” she said. Ilori announced that NACA would unveil the National HIV Domestic Resource Mobilisation and Sustainability Strategy 2026–2030 on Dec. 1, as part of the World AIDS Day commemoration. According to her, the strategy will strengthen domestic financing, promote national ownership and sustain Nigeria’s HIV response amid declining global health funding. She also announced plans for a National Prevention Conference to explore innovative HIV prevention approaches, including self-testing, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and emerging prevention technologies. Dr Adebobola Bashorun, National Coordinator, National AIDS, Viral Hepatitis and STIs Control Programme (NASCP), said innovations would only save lives if they were accessible and affordable. “We can have the best technology and products, but without access they are useless,” he said. Bashorun said Nigeria was scaling up injectable HIV prevention medicines, oral PrEP and interventions to prevent mother-to-child transmission. UNAIDS Country Director, Ms Tina Boonto, said more than 1.5 million Nigerians living with HIV were accessing antiretroviral treatment. She, however, said Nigeria recorded about 64,000 new HIV infections annually, far above the fewer than 5,000 required to end AIDS as a public health threat. “Ending AIDS starts with ensuring everyone can access the services, medicines, technologies and information they need,” she said. Boonto called for increased HIV testing, expanded prevention services and stronger efforts to eliminate mother-to-child transmission. item.title: Four die as Omo-Agege survives alleged assassination attempt in Delta
item.description: By Efe Onodjae Former Deputy Senate President and Delta Central senatorial candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, has survived an alleged assassination attempt during a campaign tour of Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. The attack, which occurred during a campaign visit, reportedly left four persons dead and four others critically injured. The Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation, in a statement by its Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, said armed men opened fire on the senator and his entourage at close range while he was addressing a crowd that had gathered to receive him. According to the organisation, Omo-Agege escaped being hit by bullets, which allegedly passed close to his head. It identified two of the deceased as its aides, Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro. The statement also named the injured as Chief Evance Ivwurie, Chuks Erhire, Tobore Agba and Ayodo Wanogho, adding that they were receiving medical attention. The organisation said eyewitnesses alleged that the attackers were heard shouting, “It’s Omo-Agege we want to kill,” describing the incident as a targeted assassination attempt rather than a political clash. However, a video obtained by Vanguard showed some NDC supporters lying bloodied on the floor of a hospital. When Vanguard contacted some eyewitnesses, one of them, Pius Eguono, said, “We were all shot in the crowd, but Efemena Umukoro has been killed. item.title: Tinubu, Sanwo-Olu court Igbo community ahead of 2027 polls
item.description: …Urge national cohesion, economic inclusion By Olasunkanmi Akoni President Bola Tinubu and Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, have urged Nigerians to rise above ethnic and regional divisions, emphasising the need for national cohesion, mutual understanding and inclusive economic development. The leaders made the call on Monday at the Ndigbo Lagos State Town Hall, organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiative (NNDDI) at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly the National Arts Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos. The engagement, attended by Igbo community leaders, business stakeholders and government officials, provided an opportunity to strengthen relations between the Igbo community and the Lagos and Federal Governments ahead of the 2027 general elections. Addressing participants, Tinubu urged Nigerians to embrace a shared national identity, irrespective of their ethnic, religious or regional backgrounds, saying the country’s development depended on the collective contributions of all citizens. He also stressed the importance of creating broad-based economic opportunities to enable Nigerians to contribute meaningfully to nation-building. “We must see ourselves as one people with a shared future. “Nigeria must rise above its divisions, because our true development depends on the active participation and commitment of every single citizen, regardless of background,” the President said. Earlier, Sanwo-Olu commended Tinubu for attending the gathering, describing his presence as an affirmation of the important role played by the Igbo community in the socioeconomic development of Lagos State. He acknowledged the contributions of Igbo political leaders, entrepreneurs, business associates and other stakeholders to the growth of the state. “The President’s presence here today is a significant gesture of recognition for Ndigbo and their rightful place in Lagos. “We deeply value the enduring contributions and longstanding partnerships of the political leaders, business associates, and stakeholders who continue to build this state alongside us,” the governor said. Reflecting on Nigeria’s democratic journey, particularly the political developments of 1999, 2003 and 2007, Sanwo-Olu also paid tribute to past and present leaders whose contributions helped shape the country’s political evolution. The town hall was designed to deepen engagement, address concerns affecting the Igbo community in Lagos and strengthen collaboration between community representatives and the two tiers of government. item.title: Obi Meets Niger State Residents, Urges Nigerians To Turn Out For 2027 Elections
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged Nigerians to turn out en masse for the 2027 general elections and remain at their polling units until their votes are counted and transmitted. Obi made the call during a campaign visit to Suleja, Niger State, where he urged voters to resist attempts to manipulate the outcome of the elections by ensuring that their votes were properly accounted for. He also criticised President Bola Tinubu, claiming that the president lacked the physical strength required to govern the country and was more interested in retaining power for personal gains than serving Nigerians. Obi, who is seeking the presidency for the second time, also promised to address Nigeria’s electricity challenges, pledging that his administration would generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000 megawatts of electricity if elected. Niger residents gather for an engagement of NDC Presidential candidate Peter Obi. Photo: NigeriaNDCHQ/X He said Niger State would play a role in achieving the target, citing the state’s resources as part of the potential support for his proposed power-sector plan. The former Anambra State governor has been holding town hall meetings and engaging residents in different states ahead of the 2027 general elections. NDC Presidential candidate Peter Obi. Photo: NigeriaNDCHQ/X Obi contested the 2023 presidential election under the Labour Party, finishing third with 6,101,533 votes, behind Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, who polled 8,794,726 votes, and Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, who received 6,984,520 votes. Tinubu is seeking re-election in 2027, while Obi is contesting under the NDC. Ahead of the election, major contenders include Tinubu under the APC, Atiku of the ADC, and Obi of the NDC. Other parties include the AAC, PDP, APM, SDP, PRP, Labour Party, and YPP. The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections are slated for February 6, 2027.
